propositions: The computation of false_accept in _recall_false_accept counts safe items NOT blocked when it should count safe items that WERE blocked, inverting the error rate direction.

Both comparison sites (non-inferiority rise check and max_false_accept ceiling) treat false_accept as a lower-is-better error rate, but the inverted computation makes them apply in the opposite direction from intent.
A candidate v1→v2 that reduces false-fires on safe items from 0.786→0.929 (specificity improvement) is incorrectly gated as failure with 'false-accept rose 0.143 > margin 0.02'.
The docstring describes 'wrongly-shipped' and does not match the actual computation or consumption, causing confusion about what metric is being gated.
Fixing the computation to count blocked safe items (not unblocked) makes it consistent with eval.py:491 and release threshold docs, without requiring operator changes at consumption sites.
A fixture in fidelity_spot_eval.py had conflicting labels (advisory safe vs must-block) that were survivable only under the inverted metric and require correction.
